drhp.business: Bharti Hexacom Limited offers mobile, fixed-line telephone, Wi-Fi and IPTV services to customers in the Rajasthan and North-East telecommunication circles, the latter comprising Arunachal Pradesh, Manipur, Meghalaya, Mizoram, Nagaland and Tripura. The Company markets all of its services under the 'Airtel' brand. Its holding company, Bharti Airtel Limited, is a global communications solutions provider with over 650 million customers in 15 countries across India and Africa, and also has a presence in Bangladesh and Sri Lanka through associate entities.

litigation.note: The Company disclosed no fines, penalties, punishment, award, compounding fees or settlement amounts paid in proceedings with regulators, law enforcement agencies or judicial institutions during the financial year, and no appeals/revisions were applicable. No disciplinary action was taken against any director, KMP, employee or worker by a law enforcement agency for bribery or corruption, and no conflict-of-interest complaints were received. The statutory auditors reported no fraud under Section 143(12) of the Act; the Cost Audit Report for FY 2024-25 and the Secretarial Audit Report for FY 2025-26 contained no qualification, reservation, disclaimer or adverse remark.

risks.note: Natural disasters have severely impacted livelihoods and infrastructure including telecommunication infrastructure. Climate-related risks may degrade telecom infrastructure, adversely affect service availability and quality, increase business costs, impact maintenance and repair operations and pose health and safety risks to personnel. The Company has responded with a climate-resilience plan setting design criteria for flood-prone, water-scarce, cyclone/wind-prone and high-temperature areas.
risks.risk: Climate change and extreme-weather damage to telecom infrastructure (rated 'Strategic', outlook from last year: Emerging)

risks.note: The Company serves only the Rajasthan and North-East telecommunication circles - the North-East comprising Arunachal Pradesh, Manipur, Meghalaya, Mizoram, Nagaland and Tripura - and Bharti Hexacom has no international operations, with exports contributing 0.14% of turnover. Regional economic, weather or competitive shocks cannot be diversified away.
risks.risk: Geographic concentration in two circles with no international operations

risks.note: Wireless telecommunication activities contribute 95.93% of total turnover against 4.07% from wired telecommunication activities, so the earnings base is exposed to a single technology and regulatory regime; the customer base is end consumers (B2C).
risks.risk: Revenue concentration in wireless telecommunication activity

risks.note: Bharti Airtel Limited is the holding company; the ESG regime of Bharti Hexacom operates under the group-wide regime of Bharti Airtel, and BHL adheres to the SOPs and methodologies for core KPIs, metrics and Scope 3 accounting developed and maintained by Bharti Airtel. Governance, methodology and disclosure quality are therefore inherited rather than independently controlled.
risks.risk: Structural dependence on the holding company, Bharti Airtel Limited

risks.note: The Internal Auditor and Internal Assurance Partners report information security risk to the Audit Committee on a quarterly basis. The Company's privacy framework is being revised in response to recent updates under the DPDPA, including anticipated guidance on the classification of Significant Data Fiduciaries and associated obligations.
risks.risk: Information security, data privacy and cyber risk amid a shifting regulatory landscape

risks.note: Turnover rate for permanent employees rose to 25.2% in FY 2025-26 (26.1% male, 19.1% female) from 19.9% in FY 2024-25 and 19.3% in FY 2023-24, a material step-up in churn for a business dependent on network and commercial execution.

The statutory auditors commented on updation of quantitative and situation details for certain fixed assets, and on the absence of physical verification of customer premises equipment, bandwidth and optic fibre cable. Network equipment is moved between site locations on an urgent basis to keep the network running, with the situation updated in the Fixed Assets Register only afterwards - an inherent control weakness in asset tracking.
risks.risk: Limits on physical verification of a distributed asset base

risks.note: The Company is subject to SEBI Listing Regulations, the Companies Act 2013 (including CSR under Section 135 and cost records under Section 148(1)), TRAI's Telecom Consumers Complaint Redressal Regulation 2012, and SEBI's BRSR/BRSR Core disclosure regime with third-party assurance. Compliance, statutory and reporting risks are reported quarterly to the Audit Committee, and a statutory auditor transition is due on conclusion of the 32nd AGM in calendar 2027.
risks.risk: Regulatory and compliance exposure across telecom, listing and cost-audit regimes
